topics.name: Uses of could and other modals
Prepositions of time, place and movement

options: Aryan ordered a ice cream after lunch.
Aryan ordered an ice creams after lunch.
Aryan ordered an ice cream after lunch.
questions.rule: an comes before a vowel sound (an ice cream), and an is used only with a singular noun.
An adverb (brightly) tells us how she greeted them.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Use at with clock times: at half past six.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A verb (placed) is described by an adverb: carefully.
expensive begins with a vowel sound, so use an.
could shows ability in the past (when she was young).
Reported statement: said that + subject + past tense verb (was).

options: Could I helped you with it?
Could I help you with it?
Could I helping you with it?
questions.rule: A modal like could is always followed by the base verb: could I help.

questions.source: She said, "I never eat anything for luncheon."
options: She told that she never ate anything for luncheon.
She said that I never ate anything for luncheon.
She said that she never ate anything for luncheon.
questions.rule: said that; I becomes she; present eat moves back to ate. told needs an object.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Live in a city; an adverb (barely) describes the adjective enough.

options: Could you pass me the menu, please?
Could you passed me the menu, please?
Could you to pass me the menu, please?
questions.rule: Could you + base verb (pass) makes a polite request.

options: The waiter came up to our table with a basket of peaches.
The waiter came up at our table with a basket of peaches.
The waiter came up to our table by a basket of peaches.
questions.rule: Movement towards a place: came up to; carrying something: with a basket.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: An adjective (expensive) is described by an adverb: horribly expensive.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: told takes a person straight after it: told me. We say said to me or spoke to me, never 'spoke me'.
The fixed phrase is catch sight of someone.
Could you + base verb + object + please?

options: I would like an cup of coffee and an ice cream.
I would like a cup of coffee and an ice cream.
I would like a cup of coffee and a ice cream.
questions.rule: a before a consonant sound (a cup), an before a vowel sound (an ice cream).

chat: What did the doctor tell you?
options: He told me drink more water.
He told to me drink more water.
He told me to drink more water.
questions.rule: Reported advice or order: told + person + to + base verb.

questions.source: The waiter said to me, "The salmon has just come in."
options: The waiter told me that the salmon had just came in.
The waiter said me that the salmon had just come in.
The waiter told me that the salmon had just come in.
questions.rule: said to me becomes told me; has come moves back to had come.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Past ability: could walk; movement towards a place: goes to the market.

options: She asked me whether was I still hungry.
She asked me whether I was still hungry.
She asked me that whether I was still hungry.
questions.rule: Reported question: whether + subject + verb (I was), no that, no question order.
The verb replied needs an adverb to tell how: generously.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: as a child points to the past, so past ability is could.
A reported yes/no question uses if or whether.
Ordinal words like first take the: the first salmon.
Reported question: asked + person + if + subject + verb.

chat: We could go to the beach on Sunday.
options: That's a great idea! We could took a picnic too.
That's a great idea! We could take a picnic too.
That's a great idea! We could taking a picnic too.
questions.rule: could for a suggestion, followed by the base verb: could take.

chat: When did your cousin arrive from Mumbai?
options: She arrived in 21st March, on the evening.
She arrived at 21st March, in the evening.
She arrived on 21st March, in the evening.
questions.rule: on a date (on 21st March); in the evening.

questions.source: The lady said to the author, "Follow my example."
options: The lady advised the author to follow my example.
The lady advised the author that follow her example.
The lady advised the author to follow her example.
questions.rule: Advice: advised + person + to + verb; my becomes her.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Verbs (talked, wondering) are described by adverbs: cheerfully, anxiously.

options: The guest said that she had read his book.
The guest said me that she had read his book.
The guest said that she had reading his book.
questions.rule: said that (no object); past perfect = had + past participle (read).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After felt we need an adjective for the feeling: embarrassed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Use for with a length of time (five years) and since with a starting point (2020).

questions.before: If I had known the prices, I
questions.rule: Third conditional: If + had known, ... would have + past participle.
Negative command in reported speech: told + person + not to + base verb.

chat: Can you come to my birthday lunch on Sunday?
options: I'd love to, but I can't. I am going in Nashik with my family.
I'd love to, but I can't. I am going at Nashik with my family.
I'd love to, but I can't. I am going to Nashik with my family.
questions.rule: Movement towards a place takes to: going to Nashik.

questions.source: The author asked the lady, "Are you still hungry?"
options: The author asked the lady if she was still hungry.
The author asked the lady if was she still hungry.
The author asked the lady that was she still hungry.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: asked if + subject + verb (she was); no question order.

questions.prompt: Rewrite using 'could' to show past ability.
questions.source: Abhi was able to perform well in his school days.
options: Abhi could performed well in his school days.
Abhi could perform well in his school days.
Abhi could be perform well in his school days.
questions.rule: was able to = could, followed by the base verb perform.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After said, will becomes would; came to our table; left it at home.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: hardly means 'almost not'; the adjective penniless needs the adverb completely.

options: The lady told to the author that she would like to have a chat with him the following Thursday.
The lady told the author that she will like to have a chat with him the following Thursday.
The lady told the author that she would like to have a chat with him the following Thursday.
questions.rule: told + person (no to); will moves back to would after a past reporting verb.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The phrase is at the sight of something.

questions.after: cause a drought in the region this year.
questions.rule: could + base verb shows a possibility. could have needs a past participle; ought needs to.

questions.after: Seine flows through the heart of Paris.
questions.rule: Names of rivers take the: the Seine, the Godavari.
Reported wh-question: why + subject + verb (I did not eat), ending with a full stop.

chat: What did your teacher say about the trip?
options: She said that we would leave at six and asked us to carry water.
She said that we would leave at six and asked us carry water.
She said that we would leave at six and asked us that carry water.
questions.rule: Reported request: asked + person + to + base verb (asked us to carry).

chat: Could I use your laptop for my project this evening?
options: Of course you can. I won't needed it until tomorrow.
Of course you can. I won't need it until tomorrow.
Of course you can to. I won't need it until tomorrow.
questions.rule: Give permission with you can; after won't use the base verb need.

questions.source: The lady said to me, "I shall enjoy a peach now."
options: The lady told me that she will enjoy a peach now.
The lady told me that I would enjoy a peach then.
The lady told me that she would enjoy a peach then.
questions.rule: shall becomes would, now becomes then, and I becomes she.

questions.source: The author said to the waiter, "Please bring the bill."
options: The author requested the waiter to bring the bill.
The author requested the waiter to brought the bill.
The author requested to the waiter that bring the bill.
questions.rule: Please + command becomes requested + person + to + base verb.

questions.prompt: Rewrite using the verb 'believe' and the adverb form of 'thorough'.
questions.source: She had a thorough belief in eating little.
options: She thoroughly believe in eating little.
She thorough believed in eating little.
She thoroughly believed in eating little.
questions.rule: The noun belief becomes the verb believed (past), and thorough becomes the adverb thoroughly.
